promise: Inspect GitHub access drift and apply the roster changes the user has authorized.
audience: Repository owners administering collaborator access from a declared roster.
trigger: Audit, preview or apply GitHub collaborator changes from a roster.

modes.name: Audit
modes.when: The owner needs to inspect access drift.

modes.name: Preview
modes.when: A roster change is being reviewed.
modes.output: A dry-run of invitations, permission changes and removals.

modes.name: Apply
modes.when: The exact access change is authorized.
modes.output: Actual GitHub operations with circuit-breaker and incomplete-roster checks.

examples.title: Fictional roster review
examples.brief: Use Team Access to explain a fictional team.yaml and prepare a dry-run access review for an explicitly selected repository. Separate additions, permission changes and removals. Keep welcome issues and AI summaries off. Do not invite, remove or change anyone’s access.
examples.before: A sync could treat omitted members as removal candidates.
examples.after: Warnings and incomplete-resolution gates make the roster problem reviewable before mutation.
examples.why: The declared roster and the proposed changes must both be inspectable.

boundaries: Native addteam remains the executable and import namespace; no coaching skill or hidden invitation automation is introduced.
Audit/dry-run may read GitHub; tests use mocks and do not invite users, accept invitations, change permissions or send welcome issues.
A removal circuit breaker is an operational limit; it does not itself authorize any access change.

marketing.headline: See who has access. Apply the roster you intended.
marketing.lead: For GitHub repository maintainers. Team Access compares a YAML roster with collaborators and invitations, shows permission drift and applies the changes you authorize through the stable addteam command.

benefits.title: Keep one readable roster
benefits.body: Use named role groups in team.yaml rather than remembering individual invitations and permission settings.

benefits.title: Review drift before changing access
benefits.body: Audit or dry-run additions, permission changes and removals before an apply operation.

benefits.title: Use it across repositories
benefits.body: Reuse a central roster or inspect several repositories while keeping the target repository explicit.

walkthrough.title: Install and select the target
walkthrough.detail: Use an authenticated GitHub CLI and select the repository that the roster applies to.

walkthrough.title: Preview the difference
walkthrough.detail: Read the YAML, inspect current access and run audit or dry-run with AI summaries disabled if unnecessary.

walkthrough.title: Apply the authorized change
walkthrough.detail: Invite or adjust the reviewed set. Sync removals remain an explicit operation with the native safeguards.

use_when: A repository’s collaborator list has drifted from the team roster.
You want a repeatable access audit in CI or across repositories.
Several repositories share a central team configuration.
not_for: Inferring permission to invite or remove people from installing the tool.
Treating a mocked test as a live permission-change result.
marketing.quickstart_prompt: Use Team Access to explain a fictional team.yaml and prepare a dry-run access review for an explicitly selected repository. Separate additions, permission changes and removals. Keep welcome issues and AI summaries off. Do not invite, remove or change anyone’s access.
marketing.output_preview:
Roster review
Additions: people listed in the roster but absent from access
Permission drift: existing collaborators with a different role
Removals: considered only by explicit sync mode

First command: addteam --help
Read-only choices: audit or dry-run
Apply: only the reviewed and authorized target set
marketing.example_note: Fictional access review. No real usernames, invitations or permission changes are represented.
install_notes: The native package and command remain addteam.
GitHub CLI must be installed and authenticated with access to the selected repository.
Start with --help, then audit or dry-run. Applying or syncing changes is a separate consequential action.
The shown virtual-environment commands use macOS/Linux paths; on Windows, use the corresponding .venv\Scripts executables.
marketing.proof_summary: Native mocked tests, roster parsing and a clean-wheel entry-point check passed. No real invitations, permission mutations or welcome messages were performed for the release checks.
marketing.next_step: Read the command help and preview a roster against one explicitly selected repository.

name: amplifier-capability-team-access
version_basis: Existing project metadata; not a new published tag or package release; an exact Git pin selects source for the shared portable installer.

native.status: Existing declared entrypoints preserved; runtime signatures, service access and installation tests remain separate evidence.

installation.scope: Shared canonical portable installer only; not the legacy repository helper or native package installation.

runtime.status: Host/caller authorizes each operation; installation is not a tool allowlist or standing approval.
declared_boundaries: Native addteam remains the executable and import namespace; no coaching skill or hidden invitation automation is introduced.
Audit/dry-run may read GitHub; tests use mocks and do not invite users, accept invitations, change permissions or send welcome issues.
A removal circuit breaker is an operational limit; it does not itself authorize any access change.

secret_names.native_runtime_inventory: See native documentation; no credentials are bundled or inferred.

dataflow.installation: Shared canonical portable installer only (https://michaeljabbour.github.io/reports/capability-installer/): read portable source tracked at the explicit Git pin and copy locally with SHA-256 receipts; no source text is transmitted. Legacy repository helpers copy current working-tree files and do not uniformly enforce Git pins, tracked membership or hash receipts. Native package builds and downloads have separate network, execution and storage flows described in their installation documentation.
dataflow.method: Caller supplies authorized context; existing promise and boundaries govern output.
dataflow.native_runtime: Provider/network/storage flows are owned by native interfaces and host authorization; these files do not enable them.

source_policy.revision: The shared canonical portable installer (https://michaeljabbour.github.io/reports/capability-installer/) requires an explicit full 40-character Git commit and never infers latest. This guarantee does not apply uniformly to legacy or native installers; the legacy repository helper is an operator-controlled working-tree copy without Git-pin, tracked-membership or SHA-256 receipt enforcement.
source_policy.repository_rename: Public identity may change; skill folder, imports, entrypoints, tool IDs and schemas remain stable.
source_policy.research: .research/market remains local and ignored; AGENTS governs refresh.

film.heading: Look before you sync.
film.blurb: In 72 seconds, Tansy the squirrel hands a key to whoever knocks, and months later nobody knows who still holds one. Team Access keeps one roster file of who gets in and how far. An audit compares it with real access and changes nothing, a dry run lists every change first, removals wait for sync mode, a typo gets a warning, and a circuit breaker stops a sync from removing half the team at once. Captions are on the player; a transcript is below.
film.note: The team, its handles and the repository are a fictional example. The film shows how the tool behaves; it does not report results.

legacy_repository.source_policy: Operator-controlled current working-tree copy. It can include untracked files and can operate outside a Git checkout; no uniform Git pin or SHA-256 transaction receipt is enforced.
legacy_repository.permissions: Review the specific command and destination; shared-installer transaction and permission guarantees do not describe this route.

native.documentation: interfaces.native, runtime_install_commands and project installation documentation, where provided.
native.source_policy: Native packaging, host composition and download routes retain their own version and provenance rules; shared portable receipt guarantees do not automatically apply.
native.permissions: Package builds may execute build tools; dependency or artifact downloads may use the network. Review the documented command, dependencies, destination and runtime authorization separately.
